title: A simple circuit: battery, wire, bulb
subject: Physics

sources.title: NGSS 4-PS3-2: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents
OpenStax University Physics Volume 2, 10.1 Electromotive Force (a battery needs a complete circuit)

steps.title: Battery
steps.instruction: Trace the battery and its bump on top.

note.text: A battery stores energy. When it's connected in a complete loop, it pushes an electric current around.

steps.title: Wires
steps.instruction: Trace the wires that run from the battery to the bulb and back.

note.text: Metal wires carry the electric current. Energy travels along them from the battery to the bulb.

steps.title: Switch
steps.instruction: Draw the switch closing the gap in the wire.

note.text: A switch opens or closes the loop. Closed, current can flow all the way round. Open, the loop is broken and it stops.

steps.title: Contacts
steps.instruction: Dab the two metal contacts of the switch.

note.text: The switch's metal bar touches both contacts to join the wire.

steps.title: Bulb
steps.instruction: Trace the glass bulb and its metal base.

note.text: Current flows in through the base and out again, so the bulb is part of the loop too.

steps.title: Filament
steps.instruction: Draw the zigzag wire inside the bulb.

note.text: As the current flows through the bulb, energy from the battery comes out as light. Energy has moved from place to place.

steps.title: Label the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

commonMistakes.Magnet: There's no magnet in this circuit. It's a battery, wires, a switch and a bulb.

steps.title: Predict
steps.question: What happens to the bulb if you open the switch?

options.text: It goes out, because the loop is broken
options.feedback: Yes. Current only flows around a complete loop. Open the switch and no energy reaches the bulb.
Opening the switch breaks the loop, so current stops and the bulb goes out.
The bulb needs a complete loop. With the switch open, it goes out.
Opening the switch just stops the current. The bulb goes out.

steps.title: Energy
steps.question: In this circuit, how does energy get from the battery to the bulb?

options.text: An electric current carries it through the wires
options.feedback: Right. Electric currents are one way energy moves from place to place. Sound, light and heat are others.
The energy travels through the wires, carried by the electric current.
The switch only opens or closes the loop. The battery supplies the energy.

options.text: Light carries it from the battery
options.feedback: Light comes out of the bulb. Getting there, the energy travels as an electric current.
